answer: One concrete defense is a slashable identity bond paired with quadratic voting: an agent locks capital to earn a vote, yet influence rises only with the square root of that stake, so splitting funds among many fake accounts buys no extra power. To sway a vote an attacker must lock a sizable bond for every forged identity, and if any are linked, the whole pile is slashed. That preserves an oasis of genuine participants; the fable of cheap Sybil accounts collapses at dawn, when the capital bill for each fake persona falls due.
